Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Brian Sevald/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images BOSTON — The Celtics will not sit Jayson Tatum, Paul George, or Mitchell Robinson when they face the Brooklyn Nets on Tuesday night. All three players — who have dealt with major injuries in recent years — are available to play after also lacing up on Monday night against the Chicago Bulls. The only players on Tuesday’s injury report are Devin Carter, who remains out with illness, and Derrick White, who is listed as probable with right hip synovitis. Celtics Injury Report vs. Brooklyn (10/27): Devin Carter – Illness – OUT Derrick White – Right Hip Synovitis – PROBABLE — Noa Dalzell 🏀 (@NoaDalzell) October 27, 2026 Robinson typically did not play in both nights of back-to-backs as a member of the New York Knicks, but in an interview with Knicks Fan TV earlier this month, he made clear that would not be the case in Boston. “It ain’t going to be the same in Boston [as it was with the Knicks]. I’ll be able to play back-to-backs,” Robinson said. “I’m very excited for that; it’s been a long time coming. Now I can go out there and play basketball, just go out there with a free mind and just hoop.” George has also made clear he’s as healthy as he’s felt in years; he badly hyperextended his knee two years ago, and never fully recovered during his two-year stint with the Philadelphia 76ers. “This summer really was a chance to continue to work: strengthen my body, strengthen my knee,” George said on Media Day. “It’s almost like a kind of rebirth, or reborn again — to be in a system, to be in a winning culture, a winning environment, and to feel good. To be able to work, to be able to train again in the summers — my summers the last couple of years were dedicated to rehab.” Tatum, meanwhile, has looked like his old self so far this season after tearing his Achilles 17 months ago. Joe Mazzulla did not specify Monday when asked how the team would manage back-to-backs. “It just depends,” he said. “We trust the sports science team that we have, we trust the competition of those guys. At the same time, our locker room has built on 1-15, 16, or 17 being able to impact winning. It’s just a combination of all those things. At the end of the day, we have to do what gives us the best chance to win. At the same time, keep those guys healthy and validate the whole locker room by putting guys in situations where they gotta win games for us.” The Celtics have gone with the same starting lineup every game so far The Celtics have used the same starting lineup in all three full-strength preseason games and in their three regular-season games so far—a loss to the Detroit Pistons, a win over the New York Knicks, and a win over the Bulls. That lineup has consisted of Derrick White, Jordan Walsh, Jayson Tatum, Paul George, and Mitchell Robinson. The Celtics play on the second night of a back-to-back after beating the Bulls 134-99 on Monday night at TD Garden. Pritchard exploded for 28 points in 21 minutes, while Tatum added 23 points, 7 rebounds, and 6 assists. Celtics-Nets tips off on Tuesday night at 7:30pm ET.

stories.title: 81-1: Week One Overreactions
stories.summary: I don’t see any more losses on the schedule – and other storylines around the league.
stories.detailText: Last week was some of the best sleep I had gotten in a long time. Climbing into bed with the biggest, dumbest grin on my face, giddily scrolling through my phone on Canis, Reddit, and YouTube, seeing what everyone had to say about just how awesome the Minnesota Timberwolves are. Seriously, it was great. I would whisper myself to sleep, repeating the mantra “82 and 0, 82 and 0…,” then dream of show-stopping sequences like Ant juggling the ball through traffic and rocking the rim, Melo doing the jump rope shuffle into a one-footed rainbow three, Beringer blocks, Kuminga lobs, TJ step-back threes, and secret handshakes that will be studied by kinesics experts and nonverbal communication researchers for decades. There were also dreams of glory, of hoisted hardware, of an “anything is possible” redux with the legend himself, KG, sitting courtside, tears of joy glistening in his eyes. One can dream, but most of these dreams actually did happen, so why not that one as well? Why not us? Yes, I know the Wolves will officially not be going 82-0 this year, and that’s too bad. I had high hopes we could get it done this year. I’ve reached out to the NBA about reviewing the tape and possibly getting that loss to Cleveland reversed. They haven’t responded, but that’s on them. Barring a reversal, just because we’re not going 82-0 doesn’t mean we can’t go 81-1, and putting the Cavs debacle aside there is still so much to be giddy about when it comes to this new look Wolves team. So let’s overreact, shall we? No single loss is going to stop us from listening to our hearts on repeat. The heart is always right. Best in the West Is this year’s Wolves squad reminding anyone else of the 95-96 Chicago Bulls? You don’t even have to squint to see that Anthony Edwards is obviously MJ, while Scottie Pippen has undergone some sort of bifurcation process and split off into both LaMelo Ball and Jaden McDaniels. Then you’ve got defensive stalwart and human highlight reel Jonathan Kuminga, the Stifle Tower Rudy Gobert, Ayo Dosunmu, TJ Shannon, the French Prince Joan Beringer – hold up… Are the Wolves actually better than the 95-96 Bulls? How is that even possible? With a small enough sample size, anything is possible. Also worth noting, in that historic Bulls season, they played their third game at home against the Toronto Raptors , and their next game on the road against…you guessed it…the Cleveland Cavaliers . Of course, unlike us, they beat Cleveland, but they weren’t on the second night of a back-to-back. Just something to consider when we’re comparing our respective places in NBA history. That Bulls team also still holds the best net rating in NBA history at +13.4. While I do think that’s beatable, I firmly believe the Wolves have a real shot at breaking the NBA record for point differential, previously held by the 2024-25 Oklahoma City Thunder at +12.9 PPG. Right now, even with the loss to the Cavs, the Wolves are second in the league in point differential at a still absurd +17 PPG, behind only Micah Nori’s Portland Trail Blazers . We love Micah, but there’s no way his team keeps this up. The Wolves, on the other hand, will, because of the power of friendship and Rudy’s goatee that Chris Finch strokes for good luck when no one is looking. If the Wolves continue to not just beat the teams they should beat, but consistently crush them, a double-digit differential is sustainable. And it wouldn’t hurt to embarrass some of our fellow West contenders while we’re at it. By the way, last year’s Melo-led Hornets team had a double-digit point differential from January 3rd onward, and this team is leaps and bounds better than that fun but flawed Hornets squad. To add to that, as those mid-season buzzsaw buzzers were just starting to take flight, one game that especially turned heads was a 27-point drubbing of the Thunder in OKC. Can we get in on that, please? Ant is winning MVP I’ve hitched my wagon to the Ant MVP train, and so far so good. With LaMelo allowing him to slide into his more natural shooting guard position, this fully realized version of Ant has never had this much space to work with. So far, after four games, he’s putting up 33.3 points per game on 72.1% true shooting. Ant has increased both his scoring and true shooting averages every year, which means…cue Disco Stu… If the Wolves go 81-1, it will be hard not to give him the nod. But if, for whatever reason, something goes horribly wrong and the team finds itself struggling to claw its way to 60 wins, I think those numbers will still suffice, and Ant will have himself his first real piece of NBA hardware. Ayo 6MOY campaign loading It’s as simple as this: Ayo is a stud, and the Wolves are going to be the best team to come out of the West. Historically, the studliest bench player on the best team wins Sixth Man of the Year. This isn’t even an overreaction; it’s just the most logical take. Jaden makes his first all-star game Your favorite player’s favorite player gets to play on everybody’s favorite night. /s Jaden will get a considerable number of player votes. What remains to be seen is how he fares in the fan voting, but with this team’s popularity having skyrocketed, I expect to see some favoritism swing the Wolves’ way. He’s more than earned the recognition. What’s more, Jaden will win all-star MVP because Ant will continuously feed him the ball, and then at some point Jaden will do this… Terrence Shannon Jr. will finish top-10 in the league in three-point percentage Hey, he’s shooting 50% from long-range. Did I see this coming? No. Is it sustainable? Yes. How so? I don’t know. Through Crunch, all things are possible. We’ve all heard the stories of TJ as a known gym rat. First player to arrive at the gym, last player to leave. It should come as no surprise that a player with his work ethic has managed to add this wrinkle to his game. I, for one, welcome our new three-point overlord. Elsewhere Around the League Miami Heat will miss the playoffs, again The Heat are bad. Like, really, really bad. It’s basically Giannis and an assortment of chips, and I guess Bam but sometimes he is so invisible that calling him out at all, I feel, is one acknowledgement too many. And by the way, aren’t you supposed to trade the bag of chips? That’s how we got Ayo. From what I’ve seen, this is a play-in team, at best. To all the talking heads out there who think the Heat will be fine: stop it. They will not be fine. They are atrocious, and after the Kalshi shareholder’s stunt in Milwaukee, I choose to bask in the schadenfreude of it all. If I go to the gym and the Heat are playing, I will watch the game while on the treadmill and declare myself an honorary member of the 2026-27 Miami Heat. Ty Jerome for Most Improved Player is a lock Who had Ty Jerome averaging nearly 30 points per game on the 4-0 Memphis Grizzlies on their bingo card? And if you did, have you ever actually played bingo before? With Ja finally gone, the Grizzlies are no longer just “fine in the West”. They’re on a roll, with Ty as the engine. He’s always been a bucket getter, but for the first time in his career he’s getting a chance to really let it fly, putting up nearly 20 shots a game (his previous high was 8.8 two seasons ago on the Cavs). From logo threes to his signature floater, there’s no reason to believe he won’t keep his scoring output at least in the low-to-mid-20 point-per-game range. And if the Grizzlies keep winning, this race is all but over. Denver is on life support I will admit to this very much being confirmation bias. It doesn’t help that the Nuggets got absolutely dismantled the other night at home by a Golden State Warriors team we all project to be pretty bad this season. But the Nuggets peaked in 2023, and they haven’t done much to disabuse that notion. While they still might win enough games purely on the back of professional horse whisperer Nikola Jokić, they are nowhere near the top-4 and should probably be looking over their shoulder at those pesky Memphis Grizzlies and Portland Trail Blazers nipping at their heels. However the regular season pans out, I’m just not buying it. The top two West teams are not who we thought they were With OKC’s devastating key injuries (Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace are expected to miss several months, if not the entire season), the sky isn’t falling for them, but it is lowering considerably and moving quickly while doing so. Meanwhile, the San Antonio Spurs ’ rather clunky start is showing us that progress is indeed not linear. Even if they are choosing to cruise to the playoffs, that could make things awfully contentious in the upper bracket of the Western Conference as the rest of the season shakes out. The Houston Rockets have been the most impressive team in the West so far, besides the Wolves, of course. I wouldn’t be surprised at all if those four teams are the ones wrestling for top seeding. Obviously, the Wolves will be sitting comfortably in first, 20 or so games ahead of the next tier of teams when it’s all said and done. 81-1 is undefeated. That made more sense in my head. Yaxel Lendeborg could be the first player to retire during his rookie season due to having lost all respect for the league When asked what contributed to his surprise decision to leave the NBA so abruptly, Lendeborg simply said, “I ain’t no h**.” Editor’s note: Technically, Gene Melchiorre retired from the NBA after his point-shaving scandal in college was discovered. Despite being the first overall pick, he had no way of fighting the story and walked away before Maurice Podoloff banned him Now, you have faces of the league convincing people to gamble their savings away on prediction markets with no repercussions. That’s sad. What are your overreactions to the first week of NBA play? Do you agree that the Wolves will finish 81-1? Have you also reached out to the league about the Cavs game? Sound off in the comments below.

stories.title: Why Knicks may not be their best right away — and why not to worry
stories.summary: The reigning champion Knicks fell to 0-3 on the new season, pointing to either violent regression or a debilitating hangover, depending on who you ask. But is the slow start somewhat by design?
stories.detailText: The reigning champion Knicks fell to 0-3 on the new season, pointing to either violent regression or a debilitating hangover, depending on who you ask. While fans and media have their theories, head coach Mike Brown points to three on-court causes. Brown blames missing quality shot attempts, lacking physicality/pace, and the combination of careless turnovers and poor defense in transition, per SNY NBA Insider Ian Begley. Everybody has their piece of the picture, but zoom out and the problem may be a short-term sacrifice that bears fruit in the long run, like one the Knicks dealt with last year. Brown was brought in partly to, and partly won a championship off, the willingness to use the regular season to experiment over trying to maximize wins. He installed a brand new offensive system, shortened starters’ minutes to save them for the rigors of the postseason, and constantly tried new players and lineups. This strategy paid off in spades. Karl-Anthony Towns as a passing hub saved their season in the first round, third-stringers stepped up all year round and Jalen Brunson - Jose Alvarado lineups closed the greatest comeback in playoff history. Coming into 2026-27, Brown has much cooler expectations, being the coach that accomplished the impossible versus the one that’d better or leave town. He’s also watched eight consecutive new NBA teams win and fail to make it back to the NBA Finals, and knows the Knicks can’t afford to be stagnant if they want to repeat. Given he has more leash and political capital than any New York coach in recent history, and both the incentives and blueprint for innovating, it’s only natural he’d go even further in using the regular season, conceptually, to prioritize spring wins over winter ones. We’ve seen it in numerous ways these first three games, perhaps contributing to the early malaise by throwing new questions at a team trying to cheat off a test from last year. Despite losing three games by single digits, all of which went down to the wire, the Knicks starters are playing about the same average minutes as they did last year. Brown has held firm with losing and bench-heavy units to see more of those combinations. Speaking of bench-heavy units, the Knicks have poured 19 minutes into lineups without Brunson or Towns in three games this season. For comparison, outside of garbage time, they played these combinations for 47 minutes, total, in last year’s playoffs. During training camp, Brown pointed to bigger offensive roles for his wings, so this trend aligns. We’ve seen OG Anunoby self-create much more of his offense. The offense in general isn’t simply what the Knicks trotted out last season. They’ve heavily leaned into their freelance motion approach over set plays to start the season, a challenge that could help explain their 29th overall offensive start. Brunson isn’t getting his usual amount of on-ball reps either, with his possession rate dropping from 45.7 percent last season to 29.6 percent this season, per film analyst DJ Zullo. This could be a factor in his poor shooting start. Brown’s even shifted the rotation in these opening contests, closing with James Wiseman as the primary backup center over Andre Drummond in their latest contest. This, along with adjusting between defensive schemes, has given the Knicks a steady flow of new looks instead of allowing them to ride the championship’s coattails. While these may make things somewhat tougher in the short term, if Brown is correct like he was last season, they’ll pay off down the line. A Knicks team that’s better prepared to make offensive plays when Brunson’s having a bad night, or rely on a deep bench cut in a pivotal Game 6, is one that’s better prepared to repeat. There is a downside, as the Knicks are looking to rebuild their mettle and regain their rhythm amid a landscape that’s changing despite familiar faces. The ring bought them at least three games of rope, but if the losing continues, the noise won’t stay quiet. Brown faced similar circumstances last year and successfully pivoted, so if that situation arose again, there’s no doubt he’d be able to do the same. But if the price for another championship is a 2-6 start in November, Brown, his team, and their fans should be happy to pay it.

stories.title: Paul Pierce — who earned $195 million in NBA career — ‘drowning financially’ in lawsuit drama
stories.summary: Basketball Hall of Famer Paul Pierce said he's "tapped out" financially amid a custody battle with his ex-wife, Princess Santiago, according to court documents.
stories.detailText: Basketball Hall of Famer Paul Pierce said he's "tapped out" financially amid a custody battle with his ex-wife, Princess Santiago, according to court documents. Basketball Hall of Famer Paul Pierce said he’s “tapped out” after his final check from FS1 in August, leaving him without a steady income amid a custody battle with his ex-wife, Princess Santiago, according to court documents obtained by TMZ. Paul — who earned $195.1 million in salary over his 19-season NBA career, per Spotrac — pays around $28,000 in child support and another $20,000 in spousal support to Santiago per month, the court docs state. The ex-couple share a son, King Rafael, who was born in February. Princes Santiago with her son, King, in April 2026. Jam Press/@lifewithprincess Paul spends around $48,000 a month in bills, including $8,000 in childcare, $5,000 in groceries, $7,000 on eating out, $3,200 on utilities, $1,000 on clothes and $3,500 on entertainment, among other expenses, per the court documents. The 49-year-old adds that he has $300,000 in the bank and $3 million in property to his name. Paul’s final check from Fox Sports came in August — and his average monthly income was $119,000 as an employee of the network. Pierce says he earned around $23,000 in September from his partnership interests in other business ventures. Paul Pierce attends the game between the Boston Celtics and the Philadelphia 76ers on October 22, 2025 at TD Garden in Boston, Massachusetts. NBAE via Getty Images Pierce is asking the court to deny Santiago’s request for $40,000 in legal fees and another $10,000 for a forensic accountant, whom she allegedly hired to review his financial records. The Celtics legend’s attorney said his client, who is “financially drowning,” would have “great difficulty” paying these fees since his Fox Sports income ended. Pierce and Santiago, an event director in Los Angeles, have been in a custody battle for months. View this post on Instagram Santiago previously filed a paternity suit in January, claiming Pierce was the father of her son. In court documents obtained by TMZ in August, Santiago provided text messages claiming Pierce ignored her throughout her pregnancy and “prioritized love interests and vacations” over their son. She asked the court for sole legal and physical custody of their child, as well as child support payments. At the time, Paul filed court docs opposing Santiago’s previous request for $30,000 per month in child support, plus another $100K for legal fees in the case, TMZ reported on July 31. Pierce hosts the “Ticket & The Truth” podcast alongside former teammate Kevin Garnett. He also hosts the “The Truth After Dark,” a weekly relationship and pop culture podcast co-hosted with Azar Farideh. Paul Pierce talks to the media before the game between the Boston Celtics and the LA Clippers on January 22, 2025 at Intuit Dome in Los Angeles, California. NBAE via Getty Images Paul worked as an analyst for FS1 after he was fired from ESPN in 2021 due to his conduct on social media. At the time, the 10-time NBA All-Star shared a live Instagram video at a poker game that included strippers and smoking weed. Pierce later revealed he was unapologetically “having a good time .” “Come on, I didn’t do anything illegal,” he said at the time , later adding, “I’m divorced. I’m retired. I’m having fun.” Pierce played 15 of his 19 NBA seasons with the Celtics and won a championship and Finals MVP with Boston in 2008. He also had stints with the Nets, Wizards and Clippers. The Celtics retired his No. 34 jersey in February 2018, after he retired the year before.

stories.title: Raptors' Kawhi Leonard out weeks due to knee, sources say
stories.summary: Kawhi Leonard is expected to miss a period of weeks due to swelling in his left knee, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
stories.detailText: Toronto Raptors star Kawhi Leonard is expected to miss a period of weeks due to swelling in his left knee, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. An MRI on Leonard's knee showed no structural damage, but both sides will use the time to ramp up Leonard. The 35-year-old had an uncommon offseason, as he could not join the Raptors until after a resolution was reached in the NBA's investigation into the LA Clippers ' salary cap circumvention case. Leonard issued a statement on X saying that's he's frustrated to be sitting out. "Yeah, it's always frustrating missing time," Leonard posted on X . "I came back to compete with this team and I'm focused on getting back to 100. Toronto, I've appreciated the love since I've been back. Returning soon." This injury is to Leonard's left knee. He has previously had issues with his right knee, having multiple surgeries for his meniscus and ACL. In a statement, the team said Leonard will be reevaluated in one week. In two games this season, Leonard is averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals. He missed his first game of the season on Sunday due to swelling in his knee. Leonard is in his first year back with the Raptors after being traded to Toronto from the Clippers this offseason after a scandal-marred conclusion to his six seasons there. He agreed to a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the Raptors after the trade. Leonard previously played one season in Toronto, leading the Raptors to their only NBA championship in 2019 before leaving for the Clippers in free agency.

stories.detailText: CHICAGO, IL - OCTOBER 24: Anthony Davis #23 of the Washington Wizards and Trae Young #3 of the Washington Wizards celebrate during the second half of an NBA game against the Chicago Bulls on October 24, 2026 at the United Center in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Washington Wizards’ 2026-27 regular season is young. And though AJ Dybantsa has still yet to make his season (and NBA) debut, the Wizards’ two established All-Stars, guard Trae Young and forward Anthony Davis, are producing the numbers fans expect. Both Young and Davis are averaging 22 points a game each, both in the top 30 for the NBA. It should also be no surprise that Young and Davis are also taking the most shots per game. That said, Davis is making only y 44 percent of his shots so far this season, well below his career rate of 52.2 percent. That said, Davis has only played four games so this percentage should move up over time. Young has started off on a hot streak with assists where he leads the NBA with 11.0 per game. Though he averaged just 8.0 assists per game last season though it was in just 15 total appearances with the Wizards and Atlanta Hawks. From the 2022-23 through 2024-25 seasons, Young averaged at least 10 assists per game though it also came with him averaging over 4 turnovers per game. This season, Young is only averaging 2.3 turnovers though four games is a small sample size. If Young and Davis stay consistent, the Wizards should be a significantly improved team this season, even if they can’t carry Washington to a Top-4 finish in the Eastern Conference. Now, we’re just waiting on when Dybantsa to get cleared for his professional debut.

The longest stretch of games Leonard missed during his lone campaign with the Raptors in 2019 was four games over nearly a week. At the time, he wasn’t listed with an official acute injury and his absence was described as load management. The Raptors went 3-1 during this stretch. In Leonard’s defence, the superstar made up for his absence by playing 37 of the final 48 games of the season. In the following year, Leonard appeared in 65 contests, the second most games he’s played in since 2016-17. During that year with the San Antonio Spurs, he played a career-high 74 games and was an All-Star.

stories.title: Kawhi Leonard is out with swelling in left knee, will be re-evaluated in one week
stories.summary: Expect him to miss more time than that, the Raptors will have him in bubble wrap all season.
stories.detailText: Toronto knew exactly what the Kawhi Leonard experience would be like when it traded for him this summer: He is going to miss time with injury concerns and load management, and the team will have to win games without him. That starts this week. Leonard is out with swelling in his left knee and will be re-evaluated in one week, the team announced Tuesday. Toronto said in its release that Leonard "will undergo a treatment and rehabilitation program to address swelling in his left knee. Medical imaging revealed no acute injury." (Leonard hasn't missed time with a left knee issue since before the pandemic, it's usually the right knee that needs management). Don't be surprised if he misses a couple of weeks (ESPN's Shams Charania called it a "period of weeks"). The Raptors will have Leonard in bubble wrap all season. At a minimum, expect Leonard to be out when Toronto hosts Orlando for two games this week, then travels to Los Angeles for a back-to-back Sunday and Monday against the Lakers and Clippers. That means Leonard will miss his only game at Intuit Dome this season. After that, the Raptors continue on the road against the Nuggets and Bucks, and Leonard may well miss those games, too. Leonard being out came somewhat out of left field: He played 28 minutes in a win at Washington last Friday, traveled to Minnesota with the team and was going through his normal pre-game routine Sunday when he became a late scratch due to his left knee. Leonard averaged 19.5 points and 7.5 rebounds per game in the two games he has played this season, both wins for the Raptors. While he shot just 32.4% in those two games, he looked like his All-NBA self from a season ago in terms of process and getting to his spots, the shots just weren't falling. With Leonard and Scottie Barnes leading the way, the Raptors have a fierce defense that can win them a lot of games — and a lot of playoff games. But that only works if Leonard is healthy, and that's the priority now.

NBA season 2026-27: Best and worst from the first week
teamStories.summary: Our insiders break down standout moments and answer the biggest questions from the first days of the NBA season.
teamStories.detailText: Plenty of intriguing storylines have emerged just one week into the 2026-27 NBA season . The defending Eastern and Western Conference champions have been shaky to begin their title defenses. The reigning NBA champion New York Knicks started the season 0-3 amid ring night drama , while the San Antonio Spurs dropped games against the Houston Rockets and Oklahoma City Thunder before recording their first win against the Dallas Mavericks , who were without Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg , on Saturday. Their struggles have allowed other contenders to take center stage, such as Luka Doncic putting up 52 points against the Utah Jazz on Sunday en route to a 3-0 start for the Los Angeles Lakers . Injuries have already started to take their toll, too. The Detroit Pistons ' Jalen Duren , the Orlando Magic 's Jalen Suggs and the Thunder's Jalen Williams all suffered injuries during opening week that will sideline them , with Williams being stretchered off the court . Our analysts looked at what has surprised them the most so far, some bold predictions for the rest of the season and which newcomer made the best first impression. Then, our reporters answered the biggest questions facing 12 title contenders based on ESPN's Basketball Power Index , which projects every team's chances of making the 2027 NBA Finals. Let's break down the best and worst moments from opening week. Note: BPI chances account for games through the morning on Monday, Oct. 26. Jump to a contender question: BOS | CLE | DEN | DET HOU | LAL | MIN | NY OKC | PHI | SA | TOR What has surprised you most so far? Bobby Marks: There is still a lot of basketball left this season, but Memphis has already stood out in the first week. The Grizzlies followed their strong preseason (3-1) with regular-season wins at home against the Utah Jazz and on the road against the Golden State Warriors and Sacramento Kings . Memphis' 3-0 record after opening week is its best start since the 2017-18 season. Early-season success can be attributed to guard Ty Jerome , who appeared in only 15 games last season, and highly touted rookie Cameron Boozer . In the first three games, Jerome has scored 45, 28 and 31 points. The 104 points trail only Ja Morant for the most points in Grizzlies history through the first three games. In the win at Sacramento, Boozer became the fifth player ( Ben Simmons , Oscar Robertson, Elgin Baylor and Maurice Stokes) in NBA history with at least 10 rebounds and four assists in their first three games. From a team perspective, Memphis is winning games on the boards and with extra possessions. The Grizzlies rank first in offensive rebound percentage, second in offensive rebounds and third in second-chance points. Overall, it's a surprising start to the season for a team that ranked 24th in ESPN's Basketball Power Index before the season. Ben Golliver: Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs didn't lose consecutive games after the All-Star break last season, so it was jarring to see them open this season with losses to the Thunder and Rockets. Oklahoma City squeezed the life out of San Antonio's offense, holding Wembanyama to 1-of-13 (7.7%) shooting -- easily the worst shooting performance of his four-year career. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson also deployed a four-guard starting lineup that couldn't slow down Shai Gilgeous-Alexander or reliably convert when dared to shoot from outside. Wembanyama found more success against Houston, but the 7-foot-4 center had a potential game-tying basket stuffed at the rim by 6-7 guard Amen Thompson . After blowing lead after lead to the Knicks in the 2026 NBA Finals, the Spurs' late-game offense and Wembanyama's decision-making in clutch situations will be scrutinized all season. The early returns have been concerning for a young team with championship aspirations. Zach Kram: I initially planned to write my answer about Mario Hezonja , who has played a much larger role than expected in Cleveland. The former No. 5 pick averaged 9.5 points in 19.5 minutes in his first two games after a six-year absence from the NBA. But then the Knicks lost at home against Orlando to fall to 0-3 after close defeats against Philadelphia and Boston. New York has lost as many games in a week as it did during the 2026 playoffs! One rotten week shouldn't cause real concern about New York's longer-term chances to repeat; after all, the team was frustratingly inconsistent throughout last season, as well, before finally finding its rhythm in the playoffs. But if you squint, there are a few early warning signs worth monitoring. Mikal Bridges is averaging only 3.3 PPG on 22% shooting, and the bench hasn't been as helpful as it was during the Knicks' title run. Those trends need to change for the Knicks to reclaim their place atop the Eastern Conference. What's the one contract situation fans should keep a close eye on? Marks: There are actually three players we should focus on. The first two are Tyrese Maxey and Anthony Edwards . Both players are under contract for the next three seasons, but have significant financial implications for the future. If Maxey and Edwards are named MVP or All-NBA (there is also the criteria for Defensive Player of the Year), then either player is eligible to sign a four-year, $304 million supermax extension next summer, with the first year of the deal beginning in 2029-30. Through the first week of the season, Maxey (28.8 PPG) and Edwards (28.7 PPG) rank in the top 10 in points per game. Maxey trails only Jamal Murray , Nikola Jokic and Zach LaVine in minutes per game. The other player to watch is LaVine. On an expiring $49 million contract, LaVine ranks third in points per game (29 PPG) for the winless Kings. If he has a strong season and Sacramento continues to sit at the bottom of the standings, will there be a trade market for him closer to the February deadline? Because LaVine's salary is more than the $15 million non-tax midlevel exception, teams over the first and second apron are not allowed to sign him if he were bought out of his contract. That eliminates the Denver Nuggets , Warriors, Knicks, Magic, Minnesota Timberwolves , Thunder and Phoenix Suns from signing LaVine. Which newcomer made the best first impression? Golliver: LaMelo Ball has delivered a much-needed breath of fresh air to the Timberwolves, who appear happier and less burdened than during a string of frustrating postseason exits. Though Ball's scoring has been hit or miss, his presence as a creator has paid immediate dividends for franchise guard Edwards, who torched the Heat for 45 points in the season opener . Despite his phenomenal talent, Edwards' turnover issues, streaky outside shooting and lack of stamina have contributed to Minnesota's past playoff struggles. Ball can help with all those issues. Edwards should be spared from some playmaking duties, benefit from higher-quality looks and encounter fewer double-teams thanks to Ball, who can make aggressive defenses pay with his range, driving ability and passing instincts. Minnesota sacrificed frontcourt depth and physicality to acquire Ball, but forwards Jaden McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga boast good athleticism and enough size to support center Rudy Gobert . Thanks largely to Ball's impact, the new-look Timberwolves have been significantly more watchable to open the new season. What's a bold prediction you'd like to make after seeing a week of games? Kram: Golden State will win fewer than 30 games. Coming off a 37-win campaign, the Warriors didn't have the highest expectations this season due to injuries and a quiet summer -- but they've failed to meet even that low bar in the early going. The Warriors are 0-3, and on Sunday, they started a lineup that looked like a group you'd see in the second half of a preseason game: Brandon Williams , Gui Santos , Will Richard , Yaxel Lendeborg and Graham Ike . Lendeborg has been one of the best rookies so far, but the Warriors have little size, little scoring outside Stephen Curry -- and little chance of contending for a playoff spot. More questions for contenders Boston Celtics BPI chances to make the Finals : 22.6% Are the Celtics living well without Jaylen Brown ? This will be the perpetual question throughout the season and likely won't be settled until it's over. Don't worry, Brown isn't interested in letting the topic go anyway. Jayson Tatum is off to an uneven start: He has played one great game, one bad game and one average game, which was Monday night in a demolition of the Chicago Bulls . Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla is leaning into depth, playing 11-man rotations and sticking to his philosophy of bombing away from 3-point range. So far, Paul George is making 50% of his long-range attempts, which will largely define how his season is viewed. He's overpaid, yes, but the Celtics didn't pay him , and they traded for him to be plugged in as a supporting piece, not a cornerstone. They also need Mitchell Robinson -- signed to be an elite offensive rebounder and good defender -- to fill a role, though he's off to a bit of a slow start. There's no gray area when judging Payton Pritchard 's start. Back to his sixth-man job full time, Pritchard is off to a strong start after recently signing a contract extension . He had 28 points against the Bulls, showing off his lightning-fast scoring ability, which is being counted on to fill some of the offensive void left by Brown's departure. -- Brian Windhorst Cleveland Cavaliers BPI chances to make the Finals : 5.5% Is there anything different about this Cavs team? The Cavs' first game of the season looked a lot like the last time we saw them. They led by 29 points on opening night against Philadelphia, primed to make a statement about being overlooked among the contenders in the East. And then ... Cleveland became the first team in league history to blow a 20-point lead after halftime on opening night. It mirrored Cleveland's epic collapse during Game 1 of the conference finals -- when the Cavs were up 22 points against New York but collapsed down the stretch and got swept out of the playoffs. So, are the Cavs truly an under-the-radar contender? Or will they keep running into the same wall, despite winning at least 48 games in three of the past four seasons? -- Jamal Collier Denver Nuggets BPI chances to make the Finals : 3.2% Where else can the Nuggets find some depth on the roster? The Nuggets are paying a combined $187 million to their starting lineup, leaving little for the reserves. Those financial restraints led them to a summer trade of Peyton Watson to Cleveland for a draft pick and no players in return, creating a larger need on the wing. DeMar DeRozan arrived on a veteran minimum contract and has been productive in his first week in Denver, scoring 25 combined in 52 minutes. But the first-week revelation has been Trevon Brazile , the rookie the Nuggets drafted No. 35 out of Arkansas. In a frantic overtime win over the New Orleans Pelicans , Brazile made a handful of spectacular plays down the stretch, including two huge putbacks, a crucial steal in the final minute of regulation, a pair of leaping blocks on attempted 3s and a massive corner 3 to seal it. Denver's decreased depth won't feel as drastic an issue if Brazile continues to pop. -- Anthony Slater Detroit Pistons BPI chances to make the Finals : 23.8% How will the Pistons handle being without Jalen Duren and Ausar Thompson ? Thompson should be back sooner than Duren, and Thompson is critically important to Detroit's stingy defense as arguably the league's best wing defender. Ron Holland II and Javonte Green aren't Thompson, but they're active -- especially Holland. Duren will be out for at least two weeks before his right hamstring strain is evaluated again. Remember, the Pistons no longer have Isaiah Stewart , whom they traded to Memphis in June. Paul Reed has earned a lot of confidence from coach J.B. Bickerstaff and held his own in his matchup against small-ball center LeBron James in Philadelphia on Sunday. The Pistons have looked more mature so far this season. -- Vincent Goodwill Houston Rockets BPI chances to make the Finals : 6.1% Are the Rockets a title contender now that Fred VanVleet is back? Absolutely. The Houston Rockets won 52 games last season without VanVleet , who suffered a season-ending torn ACL before the start of training camp. With VanVleet out, Houston employed a point guard-by-committee approach that sped up the development of Amen Thompson and Reed Sheppard while enhancing the skill sets of Jabari Smith Jr ., Alperen Sengun and Tari Eason . With VanVleet back in the fold, all those players can naturally slide back into defined roles. VanVleet won't play in back-to-backs during the early part of the season, but Houston smartly added veteran guard Marcus Smart in the offseason to fill the void along with a more developed Sheppard. -- Michael C. Wright Los Angeles Lakers BPI chances to make the Finals : 2.9% Are the Lakers for real after this 3-0 start? L.A. has the No. 1 offensive rating in the league through its first three games, scoring 125.9 points per 100 possessions. Luka Doncic is averaging 34.3 points, a tick above his 33.5 average last season that earned him his second scoring title. Austin Reaves is averaging 26.7 points, which would be a career high, on a ridiculous 60/60/90 shooting clip. Walker Kessler has made 23 of his first 28 shots and leads the league in field goal percentage (82.1%) and percentage of his points that come in the paint (92%). The Lakers' offense is humming better than an a cappella group. But L.A.'s defense hasn't shown anything yet. The Lakers rank 16th in defensive rating, allowing 112.4 points per 100 possessions. Yes, that is an improvement from last season, when they allowed 115.5 per 100 possessions. But their wins this season have come against the Golden State Warriors, LA Clippers and Utah Jazz, who are a combined 3-8 to start the season. And the Lakers had to surge back from an 18-point deficit and rely on a 52-point night from Doncic after allowing the Jazz to score 47 in the first quarter. The Lakers' awesome offense won't be enough on its own to carry them as the competition stiffens. -- Dave McMenamin Minnesota Timberwolves BPI chances to make the Finals : 14.7% What's the ceiling on the LaMelo Ball experiment? The good vibes coming out of training camp have turned into positive results for the Timberwolves to start the season. Ball has been exactly what they've needed. Edwards looks primed for the best offensive season of his career, Ball's passing has made the offense more efficient and Minnesota hasn't had to sacrifice anything on the other end of the floor, leading the league in defensive efficiency entering Monday. So far, so good, but how far can this carry the Wolves? They look like a legit contender in the West, where San Antonio has stumbled out of the gate with some offensive issues to clean up and Oklahoma City just lost one of its best players to a serious injury. Is it possible Edwards could continue on this trajectory and get into MVP conversations by season's end? Ball's first few games have opened the door to possibilities for this Wolves season. -- Collier New York Knicks BPI chances to make the Finals : 11.9% Are the Knicks experiencing a championship hangover? Whether it's contract extensions or championship rings , nothing has gone smoothly at 33rd and 8th in Manhattan. The Knicks, who ran through the playoffs, are 30th in offensive efficiency. They have had trouble building leads, let alone sustaining them, most recently blowing a 10-point fourth-quarter cushion to the Paolo Banchero -less Magic. Hardly anyone for New York is playing up to standard, save for Karl-Anthony Towns . The Knicks are shooting 32% from 3 and 41% overall. Bridges is averaging 3.3 points on 21.7% shooting -- something he's likely to shake out of but still worth noting. Eventually, things will turn, but Mike Brown put it bluntly: "Our crap stinks, it does." -- Goodwill Oklahoma City Thunder BPI chances to make the Finals : 45.5% How can the Thunder overcome another devastating injury? Unfortunately, Oklahoma City has a lot of experience in adjusting to the absences of its core players. A fractured pelvis sidelined Chet Holmgren for three months in 2024-25 , when the Thunder won 68 games and made a championship run after the 7-footer returned to the lineup following the trade deadline. A series of injuries limited Jalen Williams to only 33 games last season, and recurring hamstring issues sidelined him for most of the playoffs, a major factor in the Thunder failing to repeat. Now, the Thunder will be without Williams again for the foreseeable future after he suffered a gruesome ankle injury. Even after the offseason departures of key role players Luguentz Dort , Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins , Oklahoma City has one of the league's deepest rosters. But the Thunder lack big wings aside from Williams, and his defensive versatility will be especially missed. -- MacMahon Philadelphia 76ers BPI chances to make the Finals : 22.6% Is it time to worry about the Sixers' front court depth? Yes, but it seems that help is on the way. The Sixers' front court has been decimated to begin the season. They have two injured big men who haven't played a game: Dominick Barlow (back) and Tacko Fall (quad). Another two have missed time to start the season: Dean Wade , who missed the opening two games because of a left ankle sprain, and Jabari Walker , who exited the Sixers' third game because of a left knee injury and missed their last loss to the Pistons. It means a lot of small-ball lineups with LeBron James playing center -- a role James isn't hoping to fill often -- and the Sixers being significantly outrebounded. They've been outrebounded in every game this season, and by an average of 19.5 over their past two outings. Joel Embiid and Adem Bona are currently the team's only healthy centers, but the Sixers are hoping Barlow, Walker and Fall return soon. -- Kris Rhim San Antonio Spurs BPI chances to make the Finals : 24.8% Have the Spurs regressed from NBA Finals form? Spurs coach Mitch Johnson made the gutsy call to push forward the evolution of a new starting lineup. Finals standout Dylan Harper joins last season's starting lineup, alongside fellow guards Stephon Castle and De'Aaron Fox . Johnson knew the three-guard lineup would create some growing pains. "I understand the frustrations and the tension of it. But I do believe the players and staff have, whether it's put in the thought and time to feel comfortable about what we're committing to, and then also the patience to allow things to grow organically and how they need to be to get to where they want to get to in terms of on-the-job reps, on-the-job experience against the best teams in the world in this league," Johnson said. -- Wright Toronto Raptors BPI chances to make the Finals : 8.0% What has Kawhi Leonard's early impact been on the Raptors? The Kawhi experience is already in effect. He played in the first two games -- although not that well by his standards, especially shooting the ball -- and the Raptors won both games by a combined 53 points. (OK, this was because they destroyed the Bulls by 43 in the opener, and it warped everything.) Anyway, Leonard was a late scratch Sunday because of swelling in his left knee. The Raptors were promptly blown out in Minnesota, with Scottie Barnes going 0-of-12 from the floor in a miserable night without Leonard. It's worth pointing out that Leonard's knee issues have largely been on his right side , where he has had at least three surgeries. This latest issue is affecting his "good" knee. But the fact that Leonard is already missing time with a worrisome knee issue in the first week of the season is a developing story. And probably predictable. (Editor's note: Leonard is expected to miss weeks due to swelling in his left knee , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.) -- Windhorst

After pulling themselves out of the winless column against the already banged-up Dallas Mavericks, the basketball gods are serving them up another meatball of a matchup in the Sacramento Kings. In the recent past, the Kings were briefly getting the better of San Antonio teams for the first time since the turn of the millennium, kept at the edges of the postseason picture by a point-happy offense that made up for defensive flaws. They were a playoff/play-in team, free from the shackles of the lengthy playoff drought they’d finally quenched. Not so any longer. Tired of a slowly and steadily declining win total, the Kings have opted to tear it all down. Or, at least, that’s what I think they’re doing. It’s just so hard to tell sometimes. Either way (sample size disclaimers attached), the Kings are looking *really* bad. Through three games, the Kings are: last in Player Impact Estimate, Blocks, and Assists, 29th in +/- and Net Rating, 28th in Points Scored and Points Allowed, 27th in Defensive Rating, and 26th in Opponent Field Goals Made. Yeah, it’s just three games. But the teams that torched them were the Trailblazers (understandable) and the recently gutted Clippers and Grizzlies (uh-oh). My guess is that if the Kings and Spurs had swapped schedules, the Spurs would be undefeated, and the Kings would be last in every category. So, if you’re hoping for a competitive spectacle, you should probably watch something else. In fact, if there’s a game you’d like to be able to skip out on, I highly recommend this one. If, on the other hand, you’ve had a rough week already and you could really use a blowout win, this will probably serve as a spectacular little sweet treat. Especially if De’Aaron Fox goes off on his former team — which seems likely against a Sacramento backcourt that is very thin on guard talent for the first time in years. In any case, here’s hoping that this game ends up being the ‘closer to .500’ treat that we all hope it is, as opposed to the ‘Spurs didn’t take them seriously’ trick that it very well could be, on the first leg of San Antonio’s 2nd back-to-back of the season. stories.title: Why did Seahawks trade for Quenton Nelson? Are the Colts just getting started?
stories.summary: The Seahawks acquired an All-Pro guard two weeks before the deadline. What does this mean for them and the Colts?
stories.detailText: With the NFL trade deadline two weeks away , the Seattle Seahawks acquired All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. The 4-3 Seahawks are getting an All-Pro offensive lineman to add to a potent offense. Nelson is one of four offensive players since the 1970 merger to be selected to the Pro Bowl in each of their first eight seasons. The others are Pro Football Hall of Famers -- running back Franco Harris, running back Barry Sanders and offensive tackle Joe Thomas, according to Elias Sports Bureau. The 2-5 Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard last week, which promptly thrust key players into trade speculation. Nelson was the first one to be dealt, but hours later Indianapolis sent DT DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 fourth-round draft pick . We asked ESPN NFL Nation Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson and Colts reporter Stephen Holder, plus NFL draft analyst Jordan Reid, how this trade impacts the Seahawks and the Colts. Why did the Seahawks trade for Nelson? Seattle's offensive line has not been a glaring weakness this season, but it hasn't been the strength that it was projected to be after the reigning Super Bowl champions returned all five starters from last season. The Seahawks are gladly sacrificing some of that continuity to add a Hall of Fame-caliber player in Nelson, who will be an upgrade in their starting lineup over Anthony Bradford . Between Nelson and the impending returns of running backs Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet , there's no reason Seattle's run game shouldn't improve after an underwhelming start to the season, which includes a 3.9 yards-per-carry average that ranks 23rd through seven games. General manager John Schneider also has a long-standing relationship with interim Colts GM Ed Dodds -- who was previously in Seattle's front office -- and a long history of big swings at the trade deadline for players like Marshawn Lynch, Duane Brown, Quandre Diggs , Carlos Dunlap , Leonard Williams , Ernest Jones IV and Rashid Shaheed . He also has a projected five compensatory picks coming his way in 2027. So with a chance to improve a 4-3 team that's two games behind the 49ers in the NFC West standings , there was no way Schneider was going to bask in the glow of the Lombardi Trophy and sit this trade deadline out. -- Henderson How will adding Nelson to the mix shuffle the offensive line around? It will require some shuffling, because Nelson has played only left guard in the NFL since the Colts drafted him sixth overall in 2018. Grey Zabel , the team's 2025 first-round pick, is the Seahawks' left guard. The most logical option might be to move Zabel to right guard, which would relegate Bradford -- Seattle's starter at right guard since 2023 -- into a backup role. It wouldn't be an easy task for Zabel to switch positions midseason. He did play some right guard in college, but it was only three starts back in 2020. Bradford, meanwhile, could become attractive to other teams as a starting-caliber guard making $3.7 million in the final season of his rookie contract. But the Seahawks aren't hurting for 2027 draft capital even after the Nelson trade, and their O-line depth already took a big hit when Mason Richman tore his ACL in the preseason. Something else to consider is that left tackle Charles Cross is expected to miss some time after injuring his ankle Sunday night, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. The Seahawks could in theory move Zabel to left tackle -- where he started his final college season -- then move him to right guard once Cross returns. But they like their swing tackle, Josh Jones , and it might make more sense to move Zabel to right guard now and give him as much time as possible to adjust. -- Henderson Does this signal the beginning of an overhaul for the Colts, and could that include moving Jonathan Taylor ? The Colts are widely expected to undergo a roster overhaul this offseason, and it appears to have begun early. Indianapolis fired GM Ballard last week, then proceeded to fall to 2-5 with a loss at Minnesota on Sunday. That has made Indianapolis' top players the targets of other clubs' trade overtures, with several veterans in the final years of their contracts now of interest to other teams. The biggest remaining name on the roster is running back Jonathan Taylor , who is already the subject of internal conversations for multiple teams. The Colts signed Taylor to an extension through the 2028 season during training camp, but it's unclear whether the 27-year-old running back meshes with the Colts' rebuild timeline. Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner was dealt hours after Nelson to the 49ers -- the 32-year-old is in the final year of his deal and was seemingly frustrated with the Colts' current situation. The Colts acquired a fourth-round pick for Buckner. The Colts do not possess a first-round pick in the 2027 draft, making the idea of accumulating picks for veterans at the trade deadline appealing. -- Holder Are the Seahawks looking to make more trades before the deadline? As Schneider likes to say, they're in on everything -- and the extra draft picks give them the flexibility to continue looking. But even if a team has the draft capital and cap space to make an acquisition work, cash is another consideration, and the Seahawks doled out a lot of that with massive offseason extensions for Jaxon Smith-Njigba , Devon Witherspoon and Leonard Williams . They're also inheriting the prorated amount of Nelson's $16 million base salary for 2026, so they might not be able to take on another significant contract. That's notable with Taylor, a player who has been linked to Seattle, given the issues it has had at running back, but one who just signed a two-year, $44 million extension. The Seahawks have yet to see what their backfield looks like with its top two options in Price and Charbonnet both healthy. That could happen soon , as both have a chance to play Monday night against the Bears. -- Henderson The Colts add two picks here, including a Day 2 selection in 2027. What do they need in the draft? Defensive tackle and wide receiver are the two obvious areas of need. Losing Buckner makes their need along the interior defensive front even greater. Justin Scott (Miami), Tavion Gadson (Kentucky) and Bear Alexander (Oregon) all make sense for the Colts to look at on Day 2. And in a deep receiver class, Indianapolis could benefit from someone like Ryan Coleman-Williams (Alabama), Reed Harris (Arizona State) or Ryan Wingo (Texas), potentially with its own second-round pick. -- Reid

stories.title: Sources: Colts trade DE DeForest Buckner to 49ers in another major move
stories.summary: The Colts have traded DeForest Buckner to the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round pick, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
stories.detailText: The Indianapolis Colts have traded three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner back to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. This is the second major trade the Colts made with an NFC West team on Tuesday, following the trade of eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks . This marks a return to San Francisco for Buckner. 49ers general manager John Lynch has called trading Buckner to the Colts in 2020 the most difficult decision of his 10-year tenure on the job. On Tuesday, he righted that wrong. Buckner immediately bolsters an injury-ravaged defensive line on the heels of a loss in Atlanta in which the 49ers pressured Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . on just three of his 34 dropbacks. Buckner, 32, is entering the final year of his deal with the Colts and slated to become an unrestricted free agent after the season. Had Buckner signed this offseason with another team, the highest compensatory draft pick the Colts could have received was a 2028 5th-round selection being that he is an 11-year NFL veteran. With the trade, the Colts netted a 2027 fourth-round pick instead. He was visibly angry after the Colts' third straight loss on Sunday, at the Minnesota Vikings . Asked his reaction to the team's recent struggles, he uncharacteristically snapped at a reporter, saying, "I don't know. How about you guess. I'm frustrated. Same thing. We lost." Buckner remained consistently loyal to the Colts through years of late-season collapses, signing multiple extensions with the team and maintaining his faith in the roster building of now-fired general manager Chris Ballard. But his patience seemed to be wearing thin. After the Vikings loss, Buckner was asked what needed to change to help the team correct course. "I don't know," he said. "I can't tell you." The Niners (6-1) are in win-now mode as Buckner joins receiver Deebo Samuel and linebacker Dre Greenlaw as key players who departed San Francisco and are now making their way back to the Bay in pursuit of a Super Bowl title. Buckner has 4 sacks on the season, which is more than any Niners player through seven weeks and tied with Adetiwa Adebawore for most on the Colts. In San Francisco, Buckner will start alongside Osa Odighizuwa at tackle on a line that has played all or most of the season without tackles Alfred Collins (patellar tendon), C.J. West (knee) and James Thompson Jr . (ankle) and ends Nick Bosa (calf) and Sam Okuayinonu . With so many moving pieces, the 49ers have struggled to generate pressure without blitzing. According to ESPN research, the Niners have a pressure rate of 23% using four or fewer pass rushers, the second-worst mark in the NFL. Buckner is one of four players with at least 75 sacks and 25 batted passes since he entered the league in 2016, joining T.J. Watt , Cameron Jordan and Chris Jones . The 49ers originally used the 7th overall pick in the 2016 draft on Buckner. He spent his first four seasons in the league in San Francisco, which traded him for a first-round choice after the 2019 run to the Super Bowl and before he was due a lucrative contract extension. ESPN's Stephen Holder contributed to this report.

stories.title: Jerry Jones teases hiring Troy Aikman for Cowboys amid ESPN contract drama
stories.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he "could and would" hire ESPN announcer Troy Aikman to a front office role with the team.
stories.detailText: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones and ESPN announcer Troy Aikman were in the same building Monday, Oct. 26, for the Dallas Cowboys' victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football." The two could find themselves together a lot more, according to Jones, who is entertaining the idea of employing Aikman should the former Cowboys quarterback exit the broadcast booth after the 2026 season . Jones' final question during his interview on Dallas radio station 105.3 The FAN on Tuesday, Oct. 27, was whether Jones would hire Aikman for a serious front-office role. “Yeah. Yes, I could and would," Jones replied. "It’s that simple because I do think that much of him with his basic command and understanding and knowledge of NFL football. He's certainly is qualified to do any of the things that have been mentioned. "So let me make it real clear: Troy Aikman is just getting started in his life. ... I think the world of him. ... He's outstanding. The answer is not that we're necessarily going to do anything more direct with the team at this time, but don’t rule it out. It's very possible." What Troy Aikman said about working for Cowboys Aikman previously said during an interview with CowboysRoundtable.com that he would work for Jones and the Cowboys if he felt like his influence would matter in the strategic direction of the franchise. "I'm still young. I feel great," Aikman, 59, said. "I do feel there's another frontier. "I still believe it could very well be something else. And what that might be, like, I'm not talking in code by any means. I'm not real sure." Jones serves as the franchise's general manager and lead decision-maker. Stephen Jones, his son, is the team's chief operating officer and Will McClay is the vice president of player personnel. Jones was effusive in his praise of Aikman at last week's owners' meeting in New York. “Troy is very capable … He’s very capable of being any number of things, certainly with football, short of getting back out on the field,” Jones said. Troy Aikman, Joe Buck feud Aikman has said that he will be a broadcasting free agent after he and Joe Buck call the Super Bowl on Feb. 14, 2027. Buck agreed to a new deal with ESPN in September, which has been a reported source of friction between the longtime broadcast partners. The tension came to a head with an argument inside the booth that preceded the Oct. 12 "MNF" game between the Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills. Aikman's exit from broadcasting may be against his own volition if no seat or role worthy of his stature opens. He consulted for the Miami Dolphins during the organization's search for a general manager and head coach last offseason. He's served on various committees for hires of import at his alma mater, UCLA. stories.title: With two trades in one day, Colts are clearly open for business
stories.summary: The Sunday Splash!
stories.detailText: The Sunday Splash! report regarding a potential fire sale in Indy was conditioned on the C olts’ performance in their three remaining games before the trade deadline. After only one game, they tapped the "Everything Must Go" sign in the front yard. Guard Quenton Nelson, as expected, has been traded to the Seahawks. Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner has been traded back to the 49ers, as expected. So who's next? Running back Jonathan Taylor has been the focal point of speculation, with ESPN linking him to the Packers, Seahawks, Broncos, and Vikings. The Vikings got the ultimate opportunity to scout Taylor on Sunday, when he accounted for 110 of the team's 218 total offensive yards in a 16-10 Minnesota win. Taylor averaged 5.3 yards per carry and went 38 yards for the Colts' only touchdown of the day. There's an obvious incentive to maximize 2027 draft picks, especially with the Colts' first-rounder committed to the Jets as the back end of the Sauce Gardner trade. But Taylor is under contract for two more years; they may want to keep him until the offseason, giving the next G.M. the opportunity to decide whether to retain Taylor or trade him in March. Of course, Taylor would have more value now to a team that hopes to augment its roster for a playoff push. Although the Vikings were burned 37 years ago this month by the Herschel Walker trade, it would take much less than the ridiculous haul of picks and players (which became more picks after the Cowboys cut them) to get Taylor. Taylor could make a huge difference for a team premised on a stout defense. While Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason have proven to be capable options at tailback, Taylor is among the best in the league. He has the power and speed to move the chains and, when given an opening, go the distance. Whatever happens with Taylor, it's clear the Colts aren't waiting to see what happens over the next two weekends. In a deadline-driven business, the timeline for the Colts isn't being driven by the deadline. It's being determined by getting deals done now and moving on.
